$comment: The only place a design value is written. Ported from the Swift sources named in each group's `source`, or from the view source named in a token's `swift`. tokens.ts holds the expansion and documents every value kind; a token marked `platform: web` has no Swift counterpart to align with.

groups.title: Accent — one colour, adapted per appearance (SettingsAccent.celadon)
groups.note: An accent is one colour, not four. The four literals SettingsAccent.celadon spells out are a single hue at four lightnesses: the fill lifts by 0.131 for dark surfaces, and the foreground steps away from the surface it sits on — down 0.114 on light, up 0.030 on dark. That makes the accent a single knob adapting to both appearances, which is what a caller wants when they say "make it copper". Each derived token stays individually overridable for anyone who needs to art-direct one appearance by hand.
groups.swiftAlignment: The derivation is the source on both platforms; SettingsAccent is being changed to derive rather than to spell out. Measured against the literals it replaces, worst channel delta is 3/255 — fill light #6D9EA5 exact, fill dark #93C8CF→#95C7CF, foreground light #4E7B82→#4B7C82, foreground dark #9FD1D8→#9ED1D9. An emitter must therefore write the lift and contrast steps to Swift, not four resolved colours.

accent-lift.note: Only the two lightness steps depend on the appearance. Keeping the formulas themselves appearance-independent is what lets --fd-accent be set at any depth: a derived token substituted high up would be frozen for everything below it.

accent-fill.css: oklch(from var(--fd-accent) calc(l + var(--fd-accent-lift)) c h)

accent-foreground.css: oklch(from var(--fd-accent-fill) calc(l + var(--fd-accent-contrast)) c h)

groups.title: Font families — SettingsFontDesign
groups.note: .rounded and .serif resolve to SF Pro Rounded / New York on Apple platforms only. The fallback chains keep the intent recognisable everywhere else, and are therefore CSS-only: Swift names a design, not a stack.

font-standard.css: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif

font-rounded.css: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", "Hiragino Maru Gothic ProN", "Varela Round", -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif

font-serif.css: ui-serif, "New York", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif

font-monospaced.css: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

groups.title: Motion — literal durations from the SwiftUI sources
groups.note: Not from SettingsTheme.swift: these are the literals written into the view sources, each cited on the token.

motion-expand.note: Same 0.18s as the disclosure, but a different reduce-motion branch: the expandable rows pass `nil` rather than shortening, so this collapses to nothing.

motion-default.note: SwiftUI `.default`, which the selection buttons animate their tint with.

groups.title: Control chrome — knob treatment shared by switch and slider

track-off.note: No Swift counterpart: Toggle(.switch) renders native AppKit chrome, which publishes no colours. Exposed as a token for tuning.

groups.title: Window chrome — SettingsViewConfiguration and the close button
Elevation — approximations of the AppKit panel and window shadows
groups.note: AppKit draws the popup panel and settings window shadows itself and publishes no values, so these approximate the platform look and are exposed for tuning.

reducedMotion.$note: Reduce Motion collapses the disclosure animation to 0.12s linear and disables the rest outright, matching every accessibilityReduceMotion branch in the Swift source.
